newsitem.title: USA: Driver error blamed in U.S. crash that killed monks.
newsitem.headline: Driver error blamed in U.S. crash that killed monks.

text.p: Investigators said on Wednesday driver error was to blame for a crash on a California highway that killed seven people, six of them senior Buddhist monks from Thailand.
The van carrying the monks flipped over on Monday night on Interstate 5 near Coalinga, about 160 miles (260 km) south of San Francisco, the California Highway Patrol said.
Strong winds were initially blamed for the accident.
But California Highway Patrol spokeswoman Jennifer Willett said on Wednesday that investigators had ruled out the winds and now believed driver error was the cause.
"For whatever reason, he (the driver) let his car drift off and out of the lane," Willett said. "Wind wasn't a factor."
The van rolled over several times, throwing most of the passengers onto the highway. Only two people in the van were wearing their seatbelts, investigators said.
Seven people died in the accident, and seven suffered injuries. Four of the injured have already been released from local hospitals.

Six of the dead were Thai monks, who came to California to celebrate religious ceremonies at two temples. They were travelling from a San Francisco-area temple to one in North Hollywood when they crashed.
The monks were scheduled to fly home on Wednesday.
Willett said the highway patrol's investigation of the crash was ongoing.
